q: The branch of biology known as Genetics deals with the inheritance of characteristics or traits from parents to their ____.
e: The branch of biology known as Genetics deals with the inheritance of characteristics or traits from parents to their progeny. Biology systematically studies plants, animals, and microorganisms.

q: These characteristics are controlled by genes located in DNA molecules inside ____.
e: These characteristics are controlled by genes located in DNA molecules inside chromosomes. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides.

q: The physical and chemical characteristics that make up the appearance of an organism are known as its ____.
e: The physical and chemical characteristics that make up the appearance of an organism are known as its phenotype. Phenotype is the observed trait produced by genotype and environment.

q: The phenotype of an individual is determined by its ____.
e: The phenotype of an individual is determined by its genotype. Genotype is the allele combination an organism carries. Phenotype is the observed trait produced by genotype and environment.

q: Genes are unit of hereditary ____.
e: Genes are unit of hereditary characteristics. Characteristics is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Each gene is always located in the same place on one of the ____.
e: Each gene is always located in the same place on one of the chromosomes. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. A gene is a DNA stretch that codes for a product, usually a protein.

q: The different forms of each gene are known as ____.
e: The different forms of each gene are known as alleles. Alleles are different versions of the same gene. A gene is a DNA stretch that codes for a product, usually a protein.

q: If the two alleles are different, the individual is ____ to this gene.
e: If the two alleles are different, the individual is heterozygous to this gene. Heterozygous means the two alleles of a gene are different. Alleles are different versions of the same gene.

q: If the two alleles are the same, the individual is ____ dominant.
e: If the two alleles are the same, the individual is homozygous dominant. Homozygous means both alleles of a gene are the same. A dominant allele shows in the phenotype even when only one copy is present.

q: If the two alleles are the same and recessive, the individual is homozygous recessive and the recessive allele will be expressed in the ____.
e: If the two alleles are the same and recessive, the individual is homozygous recessive and the recessive allele will be expressed in the phenotype. Phenotype is the observed trait produced by genotype and environment. Homozygous means both alleles of a gene are the same.

q: Some well-known patterns of inheritance are: (i) Dominance (ii) Codominance (iii) Incomplete dominance (iv) ____.
e: Some well-known patterns of inheritance are: (i) Dominance (ii) Codominance (iii) Incomplete dominance (iv) Multiple alleles. Multiple alleles means a gene has more than two possible versions in the population, as in ABO blood groups. Incomplete dominance blends the heterozygote, as in pink from red and white.

q: Gregor J. Mendel (1822–1884), an Austrian monk, discovered laws of inheritance, based on results of breeding experiments on a ____ plant.
e: Gregor J. Mendel (1822–1884), an Austrian monk, discovered laws of inheritance, based on results of breeding experiments on a garden pea plant. Mendel used the garden pea because it has clear traits and controlled crosses.

q: A monofactorial cross demonstrates Mendel's principle of ____.
e: A monofactorial cross demonstrates Mendel's principle of segregation. Segregation is the splitting of allele pairs when gametes form.

q: The law of segregation states that during the formation of gametes, the two traits carried by each parent ____.
e: The law of segregation states that during the formation of gametes, the two traits carried by each parent separate. Segregation is the splitting of allele pairs when gametes form. Gametes are sex cells: sperm and eggs, produced by meiosis.

q: Each true-breeding plant of the parental generation has two identical alleles, denoted as either PP or ____.
e: Each true-breeding plant of the parental generation has two identical alleles, denoted as either PP or pp. Alleles are different versions of the same gene. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: Because the purple-flower allele is dominant, all F$_1$ hybrids have ____ flowers.
e: Because the purple-flower allele is dominant, all F1 hybrids have purple flowers. A dominant allele shows in the phenotype even when only one copy is present. Alleles are different versions of the same gene.

q: Random combination of the gametes results in the ____ ratio in the F$_2$ generation.
e: Random combination of the gametes results in the 3:1 ratio in the F2 generation. A monohybrid heterozygous cross gives a 3:1 phenotypic ratio in the F2. Gametes are sex cells: sperm and eggs, produced by meiosis.

q: A dihybrid cross is used to show the inheritance of two different characteristics, controlled by two genes, which may be located on different pairs of ____.
e: A dihybrid cross is used to show the inheritance of two different characteristics, controlled by two genes, which may be located on different pairs of homologous chromosomes. Homologous chromosomes pair in meiosis; they carry the same genes but may have different alleles. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: Mendel's second law (Law of independent assortment) states that during gamete formation, the genes for one trait are not inherited along with the genes for another ____.
e: Mendel's second law (Law of independent assortment) states that during gamete formation, the genes for one trait are not inherited along with the genes for another trait. Independent assortment is the random sorting of different chromosome pairs into gametes.

q: The only factor that determines how these alleles are inherited is how the homologous pairs happen to line up in metaphase of meiosis I, which is a ____ event.
e: The only factor that determines how these alleles are inherited is how the homologous pairs happen to line up in metaphase of meiosis I, which is a random event. In metaphase chromosomes line up on the metaphase plate. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles.

q: Testcross is used to determine the genotype of an individual exhibiting a ____ phenotype.
e: Testcross is used to determine the genotype of an individual exhibiting a dominant phenotype. A dominant allele shows in the phenotype even when only one copy is present. Phenotype is the observed trait produced by genotype and environment.

q: The testcross parent is always homozygous ____ for all of the genes under consideration.
e: The testcross parent is always homozygous recessive for all of the genes under consideration. A recessive allele shows only when two copies are present. Homozygous means both alleles of a gene are the same.

q: A homozygous dominant individual will produce only one kind of ____.
e: A homozygous dominant individual will produce only one kind of gamete. Homozygous means both alleles of a gene are the same. A dominant allele shows in the phenotype even when only one copy is present.

q: Backcross is done in order to achieve offspring with a genotype closer to that of the ____.
e: Backcross is done in order to achieve offspring with a genotype closer to that of the parents. Genotype is the allele combination an organism carries.

q: In the backcross, the F$_1$ progeny are mated back to one of their parents (or to individuals with a genotype identical to that of their ____).
e: In the backcross, the F1 progeny are mated back to one of their parents (or to individuals with a genotype identical to that of their parents). Genotype is the allele combination an organism carries.

q: Alleles that lack complete dominant and recessive relationships and are both observed phenotypically are called ____.
e: Alleles that lack complete dominant and recessive relationships and are both observed phenotypically are called codominant. Codominant alleles both show fully in the heterozygote, as in AB blood. A recessive allele shows only when two copies are present.

q: Coat colours of the Shorthorn breed of cattle represent a classical example of ____ allele.
e: Coat colours of the Shorthorn breed of cattle represent a classical example of codominant allele. Codominant alleles both show fully in the heterozygote, as in AB blood. Alleles are different versions of the same gene.

q: Red is governed by the genotype C$^R$C$^R$ and white by ____.
e: Red is governed by the genotype C^RC^R and white by C^WC^W. Genotype is the allele combination an organism carries.

q: When red shorthorns are crossed with white shorthorns, ____ (mixture of red and white) are produced.
e: When red shorthorns are crossed with white shorthorns, roan (mixture of red and white) are produced. Roan coat is a classic codominance of red and white hairs.

q: If a dominant allele of a gene does not completely mask the effects of its recessive allele, the organism's phenotype shows a blending of both alleles. This is called ____.
e: If a dominant allele of a gene does not completely mask the effects of its recessive allele, the organism's phenotype shows a blending of both alleles. This is called incomplete dominance. Phenotype is the observed trait produced by genotype and environment.

q: When pink-flowered plants are crossed together, all three phenotypes reappear, in the ratio of 1 red : 2 pink : ____.
e: When pink-flowered plants are crossed together, all three phenotypes reappear, in the ratio of 1 red: 2 pink: 1 white. Dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts.

q: When there are more than two alleles of the genes, it is refer to as ____.
e: When there are more than two alleles of the genes, it is refer to as multiple alleles. Multiple alleles means a gene has more than two possible versions in the population, as in ABO blood groups. Alleles are different versions of the same gene.

q: A classical example of multiple alleles is found in the ABO blood group system of ____.
e: A classical example of multiple alleles is found in the ABO blood group system of humans. ABO blood groups come from multiple alleles of one gene. Multiple alleles means a gene has more than two possible versions in the population, as in ABO blood groups.

q: The allele I$^A$ for the A antigen is codominant with the allele I$^B$ for the B ____.
e: The allele I^A for the A antigen is codominant with the allele I^B for the B antigen. An antigen is a molecule the immune system can recognise. Codominant alleles both show fully in the heterozygote, as in AB blood.

q: Both I$^A$ and I$^B$ are completely dominant to the allele i, which fails to specify any detectable antigenic ____.
e: Both I^A and I^B are completely dominant to the allele i, which fails to specify any detectable antigenic structure. Structure is the form and arrangement of parts in an organism. A dominant allele shows in the phenotype even when only one copy is present.

q: The blood group AB is referred as universal ____.
e: The blood group AB is referred as universal recipient. AB is the universal recipient for red cells because it has no anti-A or anti-B. ABO blood groups come from multiple alleles of one gene.

q: Blood group O can transfuse to any of all four groups, as it has neither A antigen nor B antigen, making it the universal ____.
e: Blood group O can transfuse to any of all four groups, as it has neither A antigen nor B antigen, making it the universal donor. O is the universal donor for red cells because it lacks A and B antigens. ABO blood groups come from multiple alleles of one gene.

q: In man, and apparently in all other mammals, the presence of the Y chromosome may determine a tendency to ____.
e: In man, and apparently in all other mammals, the presence of the Y chromosome may determine a tendency to maleness. The Y chromosome carries factors for maleness. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed.

q: Normal males are chromosomally XY and females are ____.
e: Normal males are chromosomally XY and females are XX. XX is the typical human female sex-chromosome pair.

q: Since the male produces two kinds of gametes as far as the sex chromosomes are concerned, he is said to be the ____ sex.
e: Since the male produces two kinds of gametes as far as the sex chromosomes are concerned, he is said to be the heterogametic sex. Human males are heterogametic because they make X and Y sperm. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.
